claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
The starting alloy has limited strain hardening and poor uniform deformation and fails rapidly under high-strain-rate loading.
The proposed intervention is the incorporation of approximately 1–2 vol% sub-micron Y2O3 particles into HfZrTiTa0.53.
Powder metallurgy or additive manufacturing can produce a fine, stable, uniformly distributed Y2O3 second phase in this alloy.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles impede dislocation glide in the HfZrTiTa0.53 matrix.
The nanoparticles redistribute local stress and alter shear-band nucleation.
Forcing dislocations to bypass or loop around the oxide nanoparticles increases the work-hardening rate.
The increased work-hardening rate makes deformation more homogeneous and delays localized shear-band formation.
Adding the oxide dispersion will increase the dynamic yield and compressive strengths relative to the baseline alloy.
Adding the oxide dispersion will increase uniform plastic deformation and strain before localization relative to the baseline alloy.
Adding the oxide dispersion will improve resistance to shear localization and rapid dynamic failure.
Delayed crack initiation will moderate impact-induced energy release.
At strain rates above approximately 10^3 s^-1, rapid local heating and thermal softening drive early shear-band formation.
The intervention's effectiveness may diminish at lower strain rates or under externally cooled conditions.
